items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: This was Vic Dickenson, myself, Arvell Shaw, Kansas Fields, George Wein on the piano.

ctx.x: About ten days. Yes, about ten days. And this was all new to my wife and Morocco was new to me too. But I didn't go anywhere else until when I went to, over there for George

But I had been there many times. I went and played at the World, Brussels Fair for Sidney Becket. Now this was in '58, 1958. This was Vic Dickenson, myself, Arvell Shaw, Kansas Fields, George Wein on the piano.
Now I think I remember you saying that that was a very great experience.

items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: they featured Prez and Buddy and Jo and Buck and Dickie and...

ctx.x: Were you doing a lot of stage shows then?

Yeah. And that beam would get right into my eye. And I'd have to close them, because I couldn't hardly see the music on account of this bright light in my eye. And so, then I didn't have no solo to play, so...you know, there I was. Usually in them stage shows that we had to play, they featured Prez and Buddy and Jo and Buck and Dickie and...
